about: Bee and Ross Maloof started Maloof Wines in 2015, she after nearly a decade as an aerospace materials engineer, he after years running wine programs in Philadelphia restaurants. Since 2019 they have made their wines at No Clos Radio, a vineyard and winery near Forest Grove first planted in the early 1970s, where Pinot Gris vines date to 1971. Pinot Gris is central to what they do, and Thistle is the bottling that sits in their “classic” single-vineyard, single-variety range.

The fruit comes from the Thistle Block of Haaken Lenai Vineyard in the Dundee Hills, planted in 2000 and farmed organically; the Maloofs work the only two Pinot Gris blocks on the site. Unlike their skin-contact wines, this one is a direct-pressed white. It ferments with native yeasts and ages eight months on its lees, without stirring, in neutral Burgundy barrels, then is bottled unfined and unfiltered with minimal sulfur.
Lees aging gives the wine texture and its creamy, bready notes; expect ripe apple and pear with a strong mid-palate.
